First, let's calculate ${x}^{2}\cdot r(x):$

$$
{x}^{2}\cdot r(x)={x}^{2}\cdot (-2{x}^{8})=-2{x}^{10}
$$

When we multiply the two functions ${x}^{2}\cdot r(x)$ and $s(x)$, we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }({x}^{2}\cdot r(x)\cdot s(x)) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-2{x}^{10}\cdot \frac{11}{{x}^{10}}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }-22 \\  & =-22\end{aligned}
$$
